title: Randy: Three Straight Playoff Trips, Still Hunting the Bowl
body: Every league needs a franchise that shows up, files its lineup, and makes the playoffs while everyone else is busy imploding. Since 2023, that has been Randy and The fumblers, a team whose name promises chaos and whose record delivers stubborn consistency. Three seasons, three playoff berths, zero last-place finishes. Not bad for a guy whose trade button spent two full years gathering dust.

The story starts in 2023 with a 7-7 regular season, the 3 seed, and a third-place finish, a respectable debut that included a forgettable 73.1-point dud against Kaushal in week 6. In 2024 Randy jumped to 8-6 and the 2 seed, then posted his career masterpiece: 162.5 points in week 3, dropped squarely on Ramon's head. The playoffs were less kind, and he slid to fourth. Across those two seasons he made exactly zero trades and 15 total pickups, managing like a man who believed his draft-day roster was a sacred text.

Then came 2025, his best season yet. Randy went 9-7, piled up 1,792.1 points, earned the 2 seed again, and marched all the way to Buckaroo Bowl III, only to finish runner-up while Sonny completed his worst-to-first redemption tour. He also made the first trade of his career that year, a historic event for a manager whose famous reluctance to part with players, especially anyone wearing Bears colors, had become league legend. His 16 pickups showed a guy finally working the wire, and his points total has climbed every single season.

The head-to-head ledger tells you who he has figured out and who has figured him out. He owns Brucie at 7-4 and edges Habib 6-5, while he and Kai are deadlocked at 6-6 in a rivalry that refuses to pick a side. The sore spots are Alan, who leads the series 8-5, and Sonny, who holds a 3-5 edge. Against the 2026 newcomers JMoney and Zoe he is a perfect 1-0 apiece, a small sample he will happily frame.

Which brings us to now. The fumblers sit at 3-4 with 752.4 points, and the models give them a 3% shot at the title, the bleakest outlook of Randy's career. He has already made a trade and 14 pickups this year, so nobody can accuse him of sitting still. With a 1-3 career playoff record and a Bowl loss still stinging, the question is whether this is the season the streak ends, or the season Randy grinds his way back to the dance one more time.
